statement: A mobility-one Stewart–Gough hexapod has conformal configuration-curve degree at most 28 if base and platform are not both planar, are not related by a similarity, and neither six-point set has parallel lines through disjoint pairs of points. Proposition 3.2 also proves mobility for bases with an order-three isometry cycling (1,2,3) and (4,5,6): choose platform order (4,6,5,1,3,2), scale one, and the specified three-dimensional linear family of squared leg lengths.

answer.text: Conformal degree ≤28 under explicit nondegeneracy hypotheses; Proposition 3.2 gives an order-three-symmetric family with self-motion.
answer.display: Conformal degree ≤28 under explicit nondegeneracy hypotheses; Proposition 3.2 gives an order-three-symmetric family with self-motion.

notes:
Conformal curve degree in P16 is not a generic isolated-posture count. The general liaison construction remains conjectural; the extraction separately identifies the proved bound and a proved mobility construction. It does not assert that every subfamily instance has degree 28. Migration: Merge exceptional-fibre behaviour into Exceptional locus; preserve each source result separately.
